title: Two Sum
statement:
Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to `target`.

Each input has exactly one answer, and you may not use the same element twice. Return the two indices in increasing order.

examples.explanation: nums[0] + nums[1] = 2 + 7 = 9, so the answer is [0, 1].

title: Valid Parentheses
statement:
Given a string `s` containing only the characters `()[]{}`, decide whether it is valid.

A string is valid when every opening bracket is closed by the same type of bracket, and brackets close in the right order.

examples.explanation: The ( is closed by ], which is the wrong type.

title: Reverse Words in a Sentence
statement:
Given a sentence `s`, return the words in reverse order, joined by a single space.

A word is a run of non-space characters. The input may have leading, trailing or repeated spaces; the output must not.
constraints: s has at least one word

examples.explanation: Extra spaces at the ends and between words are removed.

title: Chai Samosa
statement:
A canteen counter calls out numbers from 1 to `n`. Return the list of what it calls:

- `"ChaiSamosa"` if the number is divisible by both 3 and 5,
- `"Chai"` if it is divisible by 3,
- `"Samosa"` if it is divisible by 5,
- otherwise the number itself, as a string.

examples.explanation: 15 is divisible by both 3 and 5, so it becomes "ChaiSamosa".

title: Maximum Subarray Sum
statement:
Given an integer array `nums`, find the contiguous subarray (at least one number) with the largest sum and return that sum.

An O(n) solution exists (Kadane's algorithm).

examples.explanation: The subarray [4, -1, 2, 1] has the largest sum, 6.

title: Binary Search
statement:
Given a sorted array of distinct integers `nums` and a `target`, return the index of `target`, or `-1` if it is not present.

Aim for O(log n).
constraints: nums is sorted in increasing order

examples.explanation: 2 is not in the array, so the answer is -1.

title: Valid Anagram
statement: Given two strings `s` and `t` of lowercase letters, return `true` if `t` is an anagram of `s`, that is, it uses exactly the same letters the same number of times.

examples.explanation: Both words use the letters a×3, n, g, r, m.

title: Rotate Matrix
statement:
Given an `n × n` matrix, return it rotated by 90 degrees clockwise.

Return the rotated matrix (a new one, or the same one changed in place).

examples.explanation: The first column, read bottom to top, becomes the first row.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeats
statement: Given a string `s`, return the length of the longest substring that has no repeated characters.
constraints: s has letters, digits, symbols and spaces

title: Merge Intervals
statement:
Given a list of intervals `[start, end]`, merge all overlapping intervals and return the result sorted by start.

Intervals that touch, like `[1, 4]` and `[4, 5]`, count as overlapping.

examples.explanation: [1, 3] and [2, 6] overlap, so they merge into [1, 6].

title: Trapping Rain Water
statement: Monsoon is here. `height[i]` is the height of a wall of width 1 at position `i`. Return how many units of rain water are trapped between the walls after it rains.

examples.explanation: Six units of water sit in the dips between the walls.

title: Edit Distance
statement: Return the minimum number of operations needed to turn `word1` into `word2`. One operation inserts a character, deletes a character, or replaces a character.

examples.explanation: horse → rorse (replace h) → rose (delete r) → ros (delete e).

title: Placement Shortlist
statement:
A company shortlists the top `k` scorers of an aptitude test, but anyone who ties with the `k`-th highest score is shortlisted too.

Given the `scores` and `k`, return how many students are shortlisted.

examples.explanation: The 3rd highest score is 80, and two students have 80, so 4 are shortlisted.

title: Minimum Platforms
statement:
Belagavi station gets `n` trains a day. Train `i` arrives at `arrivals[i]` and leaves at `departures[i]` (times as HHMM numbers, e.g. `930` is 9:30).

Return the minimum number of platforms so that no train waits. A train that arrives at the same minute another leaves still needs its own platform.

examples.explanation: Between 9:40 and 12:00 three trains are at the station at once.

title: Smallest Window With All Letters
statement:
Given strings `s` and `t`, return the shortest substring of `s` that contains every character of `t` (counting repeats). If there is none, return `""`.

If several windows have the same smallest length, return the one that starts first.

examples.explanation: "BANC" contains A, B and C and nothing shorter does.
